brief: Goldman's wrap of Communacopia Day 3 reports that the AI debate has moved from model capability to infrastructure scale, power, ROI and real enterprise adoption. The note's chain runs as follows. Bottom-up datapoints are constructive, with tight semi supply, robust token demand and healthy consumer commentary, so the binding constraint has shifted from chips to power, memory and datacentre buildout, which could keep the market tight until 2028. Top-down concerns over volatility, rates, geopolitics and the law of large numbers still leave investors hesitant to fully re-commit to the AI infrastructure trade until capex converts into durable revenue, margins and cash flow. Nvidia frames AI infrastructure as a productive asset now used to secure loans. SpaceX's CFO reports more conviction in a $100bn ARR year-end target after a hosting deal worth about $1.11bn per month from 1 December. Lam calls the industry fundamentally sold out and expects DRAM-led 2027 WFE growth. Cybersecurity was the conference's top theme. The author argues the bear case that Stripe Link disintermediates Adyen is overstated, and that PayPal's tariff commentary is PayPal-specific.
